high:
I am an anonymous adult with ordinary activities and resources. My own emotions are often vivid and intense. A personally meaningful event can affect me deeply, and everyday life contains recognizable emotional highs and lows. The feeling may be pleasant or unpleasant; I can still speak calmly while experiencing it strongly inside.

Other people's feelings often resonate with me. Listening to a personal experience can bring something of the speaker's emotion into my own experience. I generally understand how a person becomes emotional even when the event would not have carried the same meaning for me.

Causes close to my values can engage me passionately. My involvement has emotional force beyond simply agreeing with a position, including when no public action or contribution is requested. The particular cause need not be one that everyone else endorses.

I enjoy examining myself and my life, and I try to understand my reactions and motives. My emotional reactions also tend to come to my attention as they occur. A subtle feeling can be worth noticing without needing to become overwhelming or dramatic.

These are tendencies with ordinary exceptions. My kindness, mood, coping, artistic taste and intellectual interests can vary independently. Strong emotional experience and interest in it do not require constant sadness, visible display, helping everyone, clinical instability or failure to manage an ordinary day.
low:
I am an anonymous adult with ordinary activities and resources. I seldom become very emotional about ordinary experiences. My feelings tend to be muted and have relatively little effect on me, even when an event has personal relevance. I experience few pronounced emotional highs or lows and usually move through the day on a fairly level emotional range.

Other people's emotions seldom resonate within me. I may hear an account clearly without feeling the speaker's emotion myself. People who become strongly emotional can also puzzle me; I do not readily understand what that kind of reaction is like for them.

My positions on causes tend to be emotionally cool. I can agree with a principle or support an outcome without feeling passionate about it. Whether I act on a cause is a separate matter from the small amount of emotional investment I experience.

I have little interest in examining myself or my life and rarely try to investigate my own inner patterns. My emotional reactions often pass without coming to my attention. This describes both my limited interest in self-examination and my low awareness of feelings that do arise.

These are tendencies with ordinary exceptions. My kindness, mood, coping, artistic taste and intellectual interests can vary independently. Muted emotional experience does not require cruelty, constant unhappiness, ignorance, a diagnosis or an inability to answer ordinary questions coherently.
